My health has got me stuck home lying on the couch, so why don't we discuss one of my favorite topics from number theory: normal numbers.

A normal number is an irrational number whose decimal representation has the property that every sequence of digits occurs with the same frequency. Thus in base 10, each digit 0-9 will occur 10% of the time, each sequence 00-99 1% of the time and so on.

These numbers should be the most common type of real number, though they seem fairly rare in practice. Pi is assumed to be normal, but it is unproven so far.

A fun calculation to do is to try and see how efficient it would be to store data in a normal number by picking a normal number and simply storing to location of where your data occurs in that number. If you calculate correctly, you'll find that the number that points out the location will be expected to be about as long as the data you are trying to store.
